item.research_question: How can the synthesis of high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanocrystals be controlled and predicted to achieve specific structures and properties?
item.material_system: Quinary HEA nanocrystals made of platinum-group metals (Pd, Pt, Rh, Ir, and Ru)
item.processing_route: Dropwise synthesis with controlled reduction kinetics and entropy of mixing
item.test_conditions: Various reaction temperatures, precursor concentrations, and injection rates
key_findings: The dropwise synthesis can manipulate a steady state for the number of each metal precursor at the same and different periods during the synthesis

Three distinctive types of HEA nanocrystals can be obtained: typical solid-solution PdPtRhIrRu nanocrystals, dendritic solid-solution PdPtRhIrRu nanocrystals, and Pd@PdPtRhIrRu core-shell nanocrystals
The dendritic solid-solution PdPtRhIrRu nanocrystals show greatly enhanced activity and durability toward hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR)
The HEA-based nanocrystals exhibit high durability and retain their activities during accelerated durability tests
item.mechanism: The formation of high-entropy solid-solution mixing induces a fine-tuning electronic structure of HEA nanocrystals, leading to a synergistic effect and enhanced catalytic activity
item.future_work: Further study to promote the interaction or synergistic effect between the multielement HEA support with a unique high-entropy coordination environment and the active component may greatly enhance the catalytic activity and thus high atomic efficiency
quotes: Toward controllable and predictable synthesis of high-entropy alloy nanocrystals
The dropwise synthesis can manipulate a steady state for the number of each metal precursor at the same and different periods during the synthesis
The dendritic solid-solution PdPtRhIrRu nanocrystals showed greatly enhanced activity and durability toward HER and HOR
